title: Takaya-Nakamura horizontal wave-activity-flux diagnostics
scientific_basis: Takaya and Nakamura (1997), Geophysical Research Letters, 24, 2985-2988
Takaya and Nakamura (2001), Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences, 58, 608-627

input_variables.geopotential_height_m: daily and 1991-2020 calendar-day climatological geopotential height

basic_state: 1991-2020 calendar-day climatological horizontal wind for each event date
flux_formulation: Horizontal stationary Takaya-Nakamura wave-activity flux on pressure surfaces

output_units.waf_divergence: m s-2, additionally reported as 1e-6 m s-2

display_and_inference.composite_field_flux: Flux calculated from the composite geopotential-height anomaly and composite basic state; used for coherent wave-train visualization
display_and_inference.event_mean_flux: Mean of event-wise fluxes; used for event-level inference
display_and_inference.component_multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR applied separately to zonal and meridional components for each lag
display_and_inference.all_event_vector_robust_mask: at least one flux component has FDR q < 0.05 and event-vector directional agreement >= 0.60
display_and_inference.persistent_difference_robust_mask: at least one component has FDR q < 0.05 and leave-one-winter-out vector-direction stability >= 0.90

event_statistics.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within primary and secondary metric families

interpretation_cautions: Takaya-Nakamura vectors diagnose the direction of quasi-stationary Rossby-wave activity under quasigeostrophic and slowly varying basic-flow assumptions.
The vectors are not air-parcel trajectories and do not measure cold-air transport directly.
Flux convergence or divergence is not automatically equivalent to local wave growth or decay because forcing and dissipation are not explicitly diagnosed.
The analysis uses daily 00 UTC snapshots rather than daily means.
Composite-field flux and event-mean flux answer different questions and should not be treated as interchangeable.
Statistical association does not by itself establish causality.
